name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
summary: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise. Applications often depend on external software to function properly. Popular open source projects that are used as dependencies in many applications may be targeted as a means to add malicious code to users of the dependency.

strategies.name: Detection of Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

analytics.name: Analytic 1823
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; Application State via Android Enterprise / EMM [Managed package inventory/status and package metadata]; OS API Execution via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: App begins first-seen network connections to destinations matching…

analytics.name: Analytic 1824
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. Correlate Application Permission via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]; Application State via Apple MDM [InstalledApplicationList / ManagedApplicationList]; OS API Execution via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: Known app begins first-seen use of protected categories (analytics, location, contacts) matching known-SDK behavior patterns post-update]. Alert on a sequence or state change…
